brief: drawSmoke's hearth term is clamp(1 - |hour - 7|/3.5) — a hard-coded hour, which LAWS names as a seasonal bug invisible to a screenshot. It lights the morning fire at 7.00 whether sunrise is at 5.2 or 8.1, and it burns the same in August as in January. Connect the hearth to the two things it should obey: the sun (key the morning on sunUp / dawnEdge, the ONE definitions, solved at the instant it applies rather than read hours ahead) and the cold (scale it with warmth and greyF, so midwinter smokes hard and a summer morning gives a wisp or nothing). The bonfire and the glasshouse already read the year this way; the chimneys are the last thing on the roofline that does not.
successLooksLike: A January morning has the chimneys working at first light, smoke the loudest thing on the roofline; a July morning has a wisp or nothing; and across the year the fire tracks the season's own sunrise instead of the clock's 7.00.
avoid: Do not touch the evening half of the light curve — #112 deliberately left it alone — and do not change drawSmoke's wind lean. The hour is the bug.
